Best New Books Coming in November 2026 for Kids and Teens

We’re so thankful for new reads!

Free Printables
By Jill Staake, B.S., Secondary ELA Education
Oct 6, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:18
Instaread

In a month that’s all about gratitude, we can’t give enough thanks for new reads to add to our pile. We’ve scoured the reviews and rounded up all the new books coming in November 2026 that seem perfect for kids and classrooms. Here’s what we can’t wait to check out this month.

  • Fiction Picture Books
  • Middle Grade Fiction Books
  • Young Adult Fiction Books
  • Graphic Novels
  • Nonfiction Books

New Fiction Picture Books in November 2026

Nina and the Missing Night by Natalia Paruzel-Gibson, ill. by Andie Lafrentz

It’s always the same—night follows day, and the world rests. But what if night never actually came? One little girl finds out in this new picture book ode to the soothing rhythms of rest, sure to become a new bedtime favorite for kids everywhere.

Buy it: Nina and the Missing Night

Endless Afternoons by Gaël Faye, ill. by Hippolyte Petitjean

The author took inspiration from long, boredom-free afternoons growing up in Burundi for this new read. No TV, no computers or video games, just the endless world of a child’s imagination to explore!

Buy it: Endless Afternoons

Good Bear, Bad Bear by Hyewon Yum

Twin sisters receive twin teddy bears, but they don’t stay the same for long. “Good Bear” seems to have no trouble staying clean and tidy just like his owner, but “Bad Bear” (and the little girl who loves him) is forever getting a little messy. Eventually, Bad Bear’s owner realizes that comparing herself to someone else, even an identical twin, is no recipe for happiness. 

Buy it: Good Bear, Bad Bear

The Snow Loves by Kirsten Hall, ill. by Marc Martin

Get ready for cold weather with a cozy new book that celebrates all things snowy! Lewis Carroll once asked whether snow loves the trees and fields, giving inspiration to this book that showcases the hushed scenes and clean white landscapes of the forest in winter.

Buy it: The Snow Loves

New Middle Grade Fiction Books for November 2026

The Horse Dreamer by Holly Surplice

After Merryn loses her father, her family plunges into a time of deep sadness, each dealing (or not dealing) with the tragedy in their own way. For Merryn, that means spending time with a magical horse seemingly made from bits of sticks, stones, and leaves. Whether the horse is real or not is left up to the reader, but the healing it brings is never in doubt.

Buy it: The Horse Dreamer

The Wondrous Tale of Lavender Wolfe by Karen Foxlee

Lavender grew up picking pockets on the wharves in this new middle grade book set in 1719. When her mother abandons her, she sets sail for new adventures on a magical but cursed pirate ship. Lavender soon discovers magical talents of her own that just might help the crew break the curse at last.

Buy it: The Wondrous Tale of Lavender Wolfe

Park Survival: Lost in Alaska by Vera Starbard

Emmett has always moved around a lot thanks to his mom’s job, but this is the first time he’s found himself in the small town in Alaska where she grew up. Here he has to reckon with a new way of life, a cousin he’s never met, and even a language he doesn’t speak. When his cousin winds up in danger due to his own bad behavior, Emmett will have to embrace his new understanding of his Tlingit heritage to save her.

Buy it: Park Survival: Lost in Alaska

Murder at Penguin Ranch by Kristin L. Gray

Murder in Antarctica? Sign us up! This new middle grade read takes mystery to the farthest ends of the Darth, where 12-year-old Nova’s mother works as a penguin researcher (though Nova wishes they could both just stay at home). When her mother’s assistant dies mysteriously, Nova has to put aside her personal feelings to prove her mother is innocent, and maybe even save her research grant in the process.

Buy it: Murder at Penguin Ranch

New Young Adult Fiction Books

Words Spoken True by Anne Broyles

In this fascinating and heartbreaking new historical novel, Cherokee author Broyles brings the Trail of Tears to life through the eyes of teenager Jane. She once dreamed of becoming a teacher but now faces incarceration, forced marches, starvation, disease, and other horrors. Jane is based on a real Cherokee girl, and her riveting story will make history real for today’s teens.

Buy it: Words Spoken True

Salt Water Blood by Manuia Heinrich

Moemoana is an 18-year-old Mā’ohi, just days from leaving her small French Polynesian island for college in Paris. But her link to heritage is strong. The sea literally speaks to her, and its warnings are dire: If Moe doesn’t leave the island soon, she’ll be bound there forever. When her younger brother Tao is suspected in his white girlfriend’s disappearance, Moe has just a few days to clear his name and make her escape.

Buy it: Salt Water Blood

Out of the Clear Blue Sky by Isaac Blum

Trish’s senator father dies when his private plane crashes in Jonny’s backyard, killing Jonny’s older sister Carmel. The two form an unexpected bond as they navigate their grief together, uncovering secrets their loved ones left behind and learning to rely on each other in unexpected ways.

Buy it: Out of the Clear Blue Sky

New Graphic Novels in November 2026

Bird! in Winter: Here Comes the Cat by Raymond McGrath

The seasons-based early graphic reader series draws to a close as Bird tries to sing the Winter Song of Friendship, but is just too chilled to make a sound. But that’s good news for Cat, who has been lurking on the edge of the story for three books now—it’s time to shine! (Pre-K to Grade 2)

Buy it:  Bird in Winter: Here Comes the Cat

Nat the Cat and the Mysterious Thing by Jarrett Lerner

Here’s a new graphic novel series for kids making the transition to chapter books, starring Nat the Cat and Pat the Rat. They use their senses to figure out what the mysterious “thing” can be, using mainly decodable words with some challenges thrown in. Perfect for classroom shelves! (Grades K–3)

Buy it: Nat the Cat and the Mysterious Thing

Yelp! Yeti! Everest Ever After by Sneha Pradhan, ill. by Promina Shrestha

When Dev and his friend Joon arrive at Everest Base Camp, they team up with their yeti friend Hiũ to help him solve a human-made problem: Mountaineers have left behind piles of trash (a real problem on the real Everest). Can they work together to find a solution? (Grades K–3)

Buy it: Yelp! Yeti! Everest Ever After

New Nonfiction Books in November 2026

North, South, East, and Gladys West by Ainissa Ramirez, ill. by Tamisha Anthony

Kids today take GPS and satellite navigation for granted, but do they know how it got its start? They will after exploring this look at the life of Black mathematician Gladys West, whose work in the 1970s helping to map the surface of the Earth led to modern GPS navigation. (Grades K–4)

Buy it: North, South, East, and Gladys West

Coretta’s Song by Doreen Rappaport, ill. by Cozbi A. Cabrera

Coretta Scott King was more than the wife of human rights activist Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. She was an amazing woman in her own right, as this new picture book highlights. Share her story with a new generation, from her childhood in the segregated South to her inspirational career after the tragic loss of her husband. (Grades 1–4)

Buy it: Coretta’s Song

My Word, Theodore! by Kate Hannigan, ill. by Stacy Innerst

Teddy Roosevelt was well known for his adventurous, outdoorsy lifestyle, but in his early years, he was often unwell and stuck in bed. In those days, books were his escape and his inspiration. This new read shares a side of President Roosevelt we don’t often see, and one well worth exploring. (Grades 2–5)

Buy it: My Word, Theodore!

Wrong Way Corrigan’s Wild Ride by Mara Rockliff

In 1938, pilot Douglas Corrigan took off from New York headed for California. The next day, he landed in Ireland. Was it a mistake? Did he do it on purpose so he could fly across the Atlantic? Discover more about the true story of a man who made history in a way he never could have expected! (Grades 5–8)

Buy it: Wrong Way Corrrigan’s Wild Ride
